title: The Lighthouse Keepers of Saltmere
key_sentences: For more than a century the lighthouse on Saltmere Point was tended by a single family.
He kept a detailed journal of the weather, the passing vessels and the condition of the great lamp.
The journal is now held by the county archive, where volunteers are transcribing it page by page.
Even so, the transcriptions already reveal a remarkable record of local life.
In the winter of 1893 the keeper noted that waves reached the gallery for three consecutive nights.
Shipwrecks are rarer than one might expect, and most entries record ordinary days of maintenance and quiet observation.
Visitors will be able to read selected pages alongside photographs of the keepers and their families.
Anyone with letters, pictures or stories about Saltmere Point is invited to contact the archive.
The organisers hope that the exhibition will encourage further research into the coastal history of the region.
Funding for the project comes from a local trust and from the sale of a small illustrated guide.
